synopsis: Town boards focused heavily this week on preparing recommendations, project budgets, and presentation materials for the upcoming Town Meeting. The Advisory Committee finalized its warrant report, recommending approval for a $240,000 water connection to two homes near the Parkerville Road landfill while opposing Community Preservation Act funding requests for a trail bridge and golf course irrigation. The Zoning Board of Appeals voted to support a proposed zoning amendment for two-family dwellings as drafted, despite concerns raised by Advisory members regarding lot sizes and septic capacity. Meanwhile, the Select Board reviewed initial findings from a municipal governance study examining town manager authority across Southborough's 68 local committees.

highlights.title: Parkerville Road landfill water connection recommendation
highlights.why: The Advisory Committee voted 6-0 to recommend Town Meeting approval of $240,000 from water retained earnings to connect two homes near the landfill to municipal water. The town confirmed it will pay for the service lines from the street into the houses.

highlights.title: Two-family dwelling zoning warrant article endorsement
highlights.why: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted unanimously to advance the two-family dwelling warrant article as drafted. Board members declined to make last-minute edits regarding minimum lot requirements across residential and business village districts.

highlights.title: Peninsula Trail bridge funding request
highlights.why: The Community Preservation Committee voted to advance Warrant Article 4 requesting an additional $217,318 in CPA funds to construct a prefabricated footbridge over Route 30. The Advisory Committee previously voted against supporting the appropriation due to total project costs reaching $428,550.

highlights.title: Southborough Golf Club irrigation system funding
highlights.why: The Golf Committee authorized up to $500 for printed flyers explaining the $1,087,296 irrigation replacement project ahead of Town Meeting. The project seeks extensive CPA funding, which the Advisory Committee voted not to support.

highlights.title: Municipal governance structure study review
highlights.why: Consultants presented preliminary findings evaluating Southborough's government operations, town manager authority, and committee structures in relation to other Massachusetts towns. Southborough currently operates with 68 committees.
